about: MUTATING — lower ONE Longhorn volume's declared count by ONE and retire ONE signed named replica, never below 2 for database or non-database data (723c0828). Requires David's passkey over plan-a-volume-replica-lowering; no previous approved operation is reused. Exact volume UID, every replica UID/placement and the complete fixed execution-source manifest are bound. Fresh running RW replicas on distinct Ready nodes/disks are required at destructive boundaries. The shared retirement engine retains disabled locality/effective auto-balance/no evictions, full growth guards, UID/count CAS, settle and exact effect readback; the named deletion carries DeleteOptions UID precondition on container stdin. Detached volumes use a bounded unique longhorn-api maintenance ticket with disableFrontend=true, never a direct volume nodeID patch or force attach. Complete claim consumer inventories and explicit live Etc/UTC daily CronJob schedules fence the whole 1800-second exclusion window; a new consumer/foreign ticket prevents destructive work. A separate per-operation cleanup owner survives the runner group or work-child kill, stops and reaps owned host descendants, and reserves 300 seconds of its 1500-second absolute budget for cleanup. Reaping host descendants cannot stop requests in remote containers: cleanup first makes a genuinely changed owned attachment annotation with exact UID/resourceVersion CAS, reconciles a losing CAS or lost ACK by rereading, then removes only its exact ticket even when foreign tickets are present. Foreign tickets are preserved; changed owned tickets or identities remain cleanup debt. Actual detached/stopped engine/replica state must read back. Every stopped operation retains a final count and all replica identities, including attached volumes; unread observations are UNKNOWN, and a snapshot cannot settle a count/delete write with unknown ACK. Host/cleanup-owner loss, unread state, uninterruptible kernel I/O, partial failure, cleanup debt or final mismatch cannot establish an effect; no guessed rollback or deletion of another replica. The source builder performs none of these live operations.
